newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel cabinet to decide on budget cut Sunday.
newsitem.headline: Israel cabinet to decide on budget cut Sunday.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanayhu and Finance Minister Yaacov Neeman will submit to the Israeli cabinet on Sunday a proposal for further cuts to the 1997 budget, a Treasury spokesman said on Tuesday.
During a meeting on Tuesday, Netanyahu, Neeman and Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel agreed to propose whatever reduction was needed to meet this year's budget deficit target.
While the three did not agree on a final figure, Netanyahu has spoken of a 600 million shekel cut.
Netanayhu hinted that he would not rule out the possibility of raising taxes to meet the deficit target, set at 2.8 percent of gross domestic product.

Asked by reporters whether raising taxes was an option, he replied: "I don't propose getting into hypotheses. We will do what is necessary to meet our target and I don't want to get into any details."
The 1997 budget has already been cut twice. Including revenue-raising measures, the government has already trimmed seven billion shekels from spending.
